title: Dentist's drill
prompt: an air-turbine dental drill mounted over a model tooth on a table with three buttons: “Air” starts the turbine and spins the bit; “Drill” moves the bit into the model tooth; “Stop” closes the air supply; see-through reveals the miniature turbine blades, bearings, exhaust and bit shaft
blurb: A miniature air turbine turns a dental bit, staged on a teaching mount over a colored substitute tooth with slowed motion and a lasting cut.
adaptations: The colored substitute tooth, bench mount and external compressed-air supply stage the cutting lesson.
Visible rotation is slowed for teaching and does not represent actual drill speed.
Drill lowers and withdraws the fixture; Stop closes the supply and withdraws the bit without repairing the specimen.
Exhaust routing is a necessary teaching-model outlet, not a detailed book-proved passage.

identity.note: The Wheel and Axle / Dentist's Drill, page 35 in both editions.
identity.mechanism: Compressed air drives a miniature turbine connected to the drill shaft and bit. The text describes ball-bearing and air-cushion designs as alternatives.
identity.classificationNote: Only The Wheel and Axle and Gears and Belts are main principle chapters in this unit. Other entries are named examples, diagrams or subsection headings. Greek Mill has both historical context and a named mechanism diagram.

adaptationDecision.reason: Retain. This uses a tiny compressed-air turbine directly at the drill head. A power drill uses an electric motor and transmission. The source itself relates this drill to horizontal windmills without claiming that the apparatus are identical.
adaptationDecision.boundary: Catalog and figure metadata establish intended scope only. No existing figure runtime was certified.

prompt.note: The proposed air-turbine lesson is faithful. The model tooth and mounting fixture stage cutting. Use the source's ball-bearing variant consistently and do not combine it with an invented air-bearing assembly. Exhaust routing is a necessary teaching-model outlet, not a detailed book-proved internal passage.
prompt.apparatusRelation: Named air-turbine drill with a model specimen and bench air supply. Keep the bearing design to the ball-bearing variant. Slow the visible motion for teaching without claiming that the displayed animation rate is the true drill speed.
